key_insight: RSI-Anything shows how an AI system can use a predictive world model to turn experience into ongoing improvement without relying on constant external feedback. It combines policy/workflow updates with checks that keep the world model aligned as the system evolves.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of recursive self-improvement when feedback is expensive, sparse, or slow, and when world-model predictions become less reliable as the policy changes over time.
method: Uses JEPA-Anything as a domain-general foundation for predictive world modeling.
Leverages the world model to guide both action selection and learning-data selection.
Applies observed feedback to improve the policy or workflow, while conditionally adapting the world model when needed.
Includes component and compatibility checks to reduce mismatch between evolving policies and predictions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical framework for building systems that improve from interaction more efficiently than feedback-only methods. It is especially relevant for autonomous agents, continual learning, and adaptive workflows where reliability must be maintained during change.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing feedback -> policy/workflow update -> conditional world-model adaptation
World model vs. evolving policy alignment chart
Icon-based flow for data selection, prediction, and validation checks
Before/after schematic illustrating improvement over RSI iterations
paper_title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
paper_authors: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu, Hao Xiao, Shuhan Xue
